newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian, Moldovan PMs say to boost economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian, Moldovan PMs say to boost economic ties.

text.p: The Prime Ministers of Hungary and Moldova agreed on Wednesday to boost economic ties from the current annual foreign trade level of $26 million.

"Moldova can promote Hungary's presence on the CIS markets while Hungary can further the Moldovan economy's presence on European markets," Prime Minister Gyula Horn told a joint news conference on the second day of Moldovan Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc's first visit to Hungary.
The first such agreement was the one signed on a joint venture of Hungarian busmaker Ikarus Rt and Moldovan company Recar.
"The joint venture will overhaul Moldovan buses and assure spare parts...and in the future could also mean the assembly of (Ikarus) buses in Moldova," said Ikarus President Gabor Szeles.
The two countries have signed seven agreements including measures to combat illegal migration and organised crime.
The fact that Moldova has opted for neutrality while Hungary is committed to joining NATO, has not caused any problems in the two countries' relationship, Ciubuc said.
"Taking into account that we have two common neighbours -- the Ukraine and Romania -- and we have the same interests... (our views) coincided completely," Ciubuc said.
